content.value_statement: Generic AI interfaces often lack visual direction and platform-aware detail. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to define design intent before building prototypes.
actual_capabilities: Defines purpose, aesthetic direction, palette, typography, and layout strategy before code.
Guides web and mini program interface design decisions.
Enforces non-generic rules for color, typography, icons, and composition.
Provides self-audit checks for generated UI code.
Suggests context-specific aesthetic directions by product type.
Coordinates with web or mini program implementation skills after design approval.
limitations: Does not handle backend, database, or API-only tasks.
Does not replace accessibility review or user testing.
May require platform-specific skills for final implementation details.
Defaults to at most four pages unless the user requests more.

use_cases.title: Shape Product Screens
use_cases.description: Turn early product ideas into visual direction, page scope, and prototype-ready interface plans.

use_cases.title: Prepare Frontend Prototypes
use_cases.description: Define hierarchy, palette, typography, and layout rules before building a web interface.

use_cases.title: Refine Mini Program UI
use_cases.description: Plan small-screen pages with clear aesthetics, platform constraints, and concrete handoff guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Design Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ui-design skill to create a design specification for [product]. Include users, purpose, aesthetic direction, palette, typography, and layout strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Prototype
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for scoped interface planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ui-design skill to plan a [web or mini program] prototype for [workflow]. Limit it to [number] pages and define each screen.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign an Interface
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for critique and redesign.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ui-design skill to redesign this interface: [description]. Identify generic patterns, choose a stronger direction, and propose a revised hierarchy.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Implementation Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ui-design skill before implementation for [project]. Produce a platform-specific design spec, component plan, self-audit checklist, and handoff notes.

output_examples.input: I need a web dashboard for a logistics team.
output: Purpose statement for dispatch planners and managers.
Industrial or utilitarian aesthetic with concrete color and typography choices.
Screen plan for dashboard, shipment detail, and exception review.

output_examples.input: Redesign my education mini program so it feels less generic.
output: Editorial or organic direction with a restrained palette.
Typography and layout rules for small screens.
Audit notes that remove centered card patterns and emoji icons.

best_practices: Provide target users, primary actions, platform, and brand constraints.
Review the design specification before asking for implementation.
Request accessibility, responsiveness, and content states when moving to code.
anti_patterns: Using this skill for backend, API, or database-only work.
Skipping the design specification and requesting immediate code.
Ignoring real brand systems when approved tokens already exist.

faq.question: Does this skill write final frontend code?
faq.answer: It can guide prototype implementation, but it focuses first on design specifications and visual decisions.

faq.question: Which platforms does it support?
faq.answer: It supports web interfaces and mini program interfaces when paired with the matching implementation skill.

faq.question: Can I use my brand colors?
faq.answer: Yes. Real brand colors and approved design systems override the default bans when documented.

faq.question: Why does it require a design specification first?
faq.answer: The specification fixes intent, hierarchy, palette, typography, and layout before code choices lock in.

faq.question: Does it handle backend work?
faq.answer: No. Use it for interface design, not backend logic, APIs, or database schema work.

faq.question: How should I start?
faq.answer: Describe the product, users, platform, key screens, content needs, and any brand constraints.
